title: Why I Changed Careers
summaryZh: 一位會計師因為義務輔導鄰居的小孩數學，發現自己真正想做的是教書。

sentences.text: For eight years I worked in accounting, and on paper it was a perfectly good job.
sentences.zh: 我在會計這一行做了八年，紙面上看來這是份相當不錯的工作。
sentences.note: worked in 的 t 連到 in 的母音，重新分音節成 /wɝk.ˈtɪn/。

sentences.text: The pay was fine, the hours were steady, and nobody ever gave me a hard time.
sentences.zh: 薪水還可以，工時穩定，也沒有人找我麻煩。

sentences.text: But every Sunday evening I would start dreading Monday about an hour after dinner.
sentences.zh: 但每個星期天晚上，大概晚餐後一小時我就開始害怕星期一。
sentences.note: would 弱化成 /wəd/；about an hour 三字連成一串，hour 的 h 不發音。

sentences.text: I kept telling myself that was normal, and that everybody feels that way sometimes.
sentences.zh: 我一直告訴自己這很正常，每個人偶爾都會這樣。

sentences.text: What changed things was a favor I did for my neighbor's daughter one weekend.
sentences.zh: 改變一切的，是某個週末我幫鄰居女兒的一個小忙。

sentences.text: She was failing math, and her mother asked me to sit down with her for an hour.
sentences.zh: 她數學不及格，她媽媽拜託我陪她坐下來教一個小時。
sentences.note: sit down 的 t 變喉塞音；with her 的 h 常常脫落，連成 /ˈwɪ.ðɚ/。

sentences.text: That hour turned into every Saturday morning for the rest of the school year.
sentences.zh: 那一小時後來變成整個學年每個星期六早上。

sentences.text: I noticed I was looking forward to it more than anything else in my week.
sentences.zh: 我發現我期待那段時間，勝過那一週的任何事。
sentences.note: looking forward to 的 to 弱讀成 /tə/，forward 的 d 幾乎聽不到。

sentences.text: When she finally passed her exam, I felt something I hadn't felt at work in years.
sentences.zh: 當她終於通過考試，我感受到一種在職場上多年沒有過的感覺。

sentences.text: So I went back and got a teaching certificate while I was still working full time.
sentences.zh: 所以我一邊做全職工作，一邊回去考了教師證。
sentences.note: went back 的 t 不爆破；got a 連成 /ˈɡɑ.ɾə/，t 變閃音。

sentences.text: It took two years, and I was tired in a way I'd never really been tired before.
sentences.zh: 那花了兩年，我累的方式是我以前從沒體會過的。

sentences.text: I now make about a third less than I used to, and I feel that every single month.
sentences.zh: 我現在的收入比以前少了大約三分之一，而且每個月都感覺得到。

sentences.text: I'm not going to pretend that the money doesn't matter, because of course it absolutely does.
sentences.zh: 我不會假裝錢不重要，因為它當然非常重要。
sentences.note: going to 口語變成 /ˈɡʌ.nə/；doesn't 的 t 在 matter 前面不釋放。

sentences.text: But I haven't dreaded a Monday since the day I stood in front of my first class.
sentences.zh: 但自從我第一次站在班級前面的那天起，我就沒再害怕過星期一。

questions.q: How did the writer first discover an interest in teaching?
options: A career test at his company
A course his employer paid for

questions.q: How did he prepare for the change?
options: He quit and studied full time
He studied while keeping his old job
He was hired without any training

questions.q: What does he say about his lower salary?
options: It doesn't bother him at all
He notices it but doesn't regret the change
He plans to go back to accounting
